# Industrial Machine Drive {#sec-machine-drive}

Most of the electricity industry uses goes to motor systems. A motor is the core of a broader system of electrical and mechanical equipment that moves liquids, air, and solids around a site: pumps, fans and blowers, compressors, conveyors, and the machines that mix and size materials. CIMS represents this equipment as a shared **Machine Drive** service that every industrial sector draws on, so that more efficient motors, speed control, and system improvements compete once and serve the whole sector.

## Structure

Each industrial sector's Service sub-tree has a Machine Drive node split into five end uses. The split follows the U.S. Department of Energy's Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints, which divide the machine-drive total reported by the EIA Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey (MECS) into these end uses; the Footprints' residual "other systems" is not carried, and motor-driven equipment that none of the other four covers is filed under materials processing.

| End use | What it covers |
|:--------|:---------------|
| Pumps | Motor-, engine-, and turbine-driven pumps moving liquids and slurries around a site. Pipeline pumping is an oil-and-gas end use. |
| Fans and blowers | Process fans, blowers, and induced- and forced-draught sets. Building ventilation belongs to HVAC, and mine ventilation is a mining end use. |
| Compressed air | Compressed-air systems and the process compression that serves them. Pipeline and gas-processing compression are oil-and-gas end uses. |
| Materials handling | Conveyors, cranes, hoists, stackers, and reclaimers moving solids around a site. |
| Materials processing | Motor-driven size reduction, mixing, forming, and separation not already counted in a sector's own process steps. Comminution, mechanical pulping, rolling, and cement grinding stay with their sectors. |

: Machine-drive end uses {#tbl-machine-drive-end-uses}

All five end uses appear in Chemicals, Coal Mining, Industrial Minerals, Iron and Steel, Metal Smelting, Mining, and Pulp and Paper. Petroleum Refining carries all but materials handling, and Natural Gas carries pumps only; its compression has dedicated compressor-drive nodes (see @sec-natural-gas). Each end use's service is measured in GJ of delivered drive energy.

## How the competition works

Each end use hosts a competition among drives and efficiency measures:

- **Drives.** A standard-efficiency induction motor is the incumbent. Where a site has fuel or steam to hand, a gas engine, gas turbine, or back-pressure steam turbine can drive a pump or compressor directly.
- **More efficient motors.** Premium-efficiency (IE4–IE5) motors, including permanent-magnet and synchronous-reluctance designs, compete with the standard motor.
- **Speed control.** Variable-speed drives match motor speed to the load instead of throttling flow with a valve or damper, which cuts the energy a pump or fan uses at part load.
- **System measures.** Leak repair, pressure and flow optimization, sequencing, right-sizing, and impeller trimming improve the whole pump, fan, or compressed-air system rather than the motor alone.
